title: GS21 with a LEVERAGE-CURVATURE exposure: one type, production x exp(-0.1 (b~^2 - 1) y), b~ the standardized coupon (hump-shaped in leverage), price 2.5
question: Does an exposure that is hump-shaped in the firm's own leverage give the oracle room in GS21 (gvy25s 11%), and does a gap follow?
notes:
WHY (2026-10-29, user: 'a firm with extreme values of leverage should be more exposed to cash flow risk'). GS21's exposure forms so far are linear in the firm's states (level, z~, z~ b~, b~), so the premium is monotone in leverage and productivity and the linear ceiling captures it (gvy25s room 11%, gvy25sq/sh 1-3%). The new term gs_bzq (b~^2 - 1), b~ the standardized coupon, makes the exposure U-shaped in the firm's OWN leverage: firms at either leverage extreme load on y, mid-leverage firms load the other way. No type is needed; the premium is non-monotone in the leverage characteristic by construction.

FEASIBILITY (gs_solve_vy.py, 2026-10-29): exposure -0.1 (b~^2 - 1) spans +0.10 at b~ = 0 to -0.20 at the grid ends (gvy25s's level exposures span +-0.1); bv_comp 0, so no level shift. gs_bzq = 0 leaves every other economy unchanged (parity: x + 0.0).

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; ids filled from the Quest build log by the solve script before any seed runs.

PREDICTION (2026-10-29): as gvyql10 with the premium a hump in leverage; room 20-40%. FALSIFIED if room is at or below 11%.

changes: one type (gs_bv -0.1) instead of six; gs_bzl 1 -> 0; gs_bzq 1 (new); bv_comp 1.2 -> 0; y_mult 2.5 kept
